title: Adjustments 1: rolling a position
summary: When to roll a short leg further out or into a later expiry, how to do it here, and why one roll is the limit.

options: Adding more of the same call
Closing it and selling a new call further out or later
questions.why: A roll closes the leg under pressure and opens a new one further away or in a later expiry.

questions.q: What happens to the old leg's result when you roll?
options: Its profit or loss is booked
It moves to the new leg's strike
questions.why: Closing the old leg books its profit or loss; the new leg is a fresh trade.

questions.q: Which new leg breaks the app's rules?
options: Delta 0.12, 35 days out, no results before expiry
questions.why: Delta 0.25 is above the 0.15 limit, and 20 days is under the 30-day minimum.

questions.q: The old leg has already reached its stop-loss. What should you do?
options: Roll it to avoid the loss
questions.why: Rolling is only for trades that still fit your rules, before the stop is hit.

questions.q: Why set a limit of one roll per trade?
options: Endless rolling hides losses while keeping the same risk
Margin can only be used once
questions.why: Each roll books a loss; rolling forever turns one bad trade into many.
